My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. The soil here on the North China Plain is good loam — it grows wheat and maize, and that is what I grow. I have about 8 mu. My knees hurt in the cold now, and my son is in Handan city, so I do not take risks with strange new crops. The grain station buys wheat and maize every year, and I know exactly what to do with them. I have been doing this rotation since I was young.

In October I put in winter wheat. I use the improved variety the seed station in the village sells — "矮抗58" or whatever is available that season. Not the expensive hybrid seed, but not the old local variety either. I apply base fertilizer before rotary tilling — diammonium phosphate and some potassium, then urea at jointing. Rainfall in spring is not reliable here, so I pump groundwater three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I spray once for weeds in winter and once for aphids in late spring. I expect about 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

Right after I cut the wheat in June, I plant summer maize directly into the stubble — no need to plough again, saves fuel. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or similar. Maize gets most of its water from summer rains, but I irrigate once at tasseling if July is dry, and maybe again at grain fill. I apply urea in two doses. I harvest in late September and sell at the station before the price drops.
